_comment: The one rule the Digital Twin and the production authority engine both implement.
simulator/assurance/engine.py says plainly that it is not the production engine and
that its rules can drift from the Go ones. That was honest and it was undetectable:
nothing compared them, so the first divergence would have surfaced as a scenario
that passed in the twin and a fleet that behaved differently in production.
Both engines read this file. A case here is a claim about what the platform does,
and it has to hold in both languages or one of them is wrong.
Only the per-order notional limit is shared. Rolling and daily limits need consumed
usage, which the twin deliberately does not reimplement, and listing them here would
assert an agreement that does not exist.

cases.name: exactly at the limit is allowed
cases.why: the boundary is the most likely place for two implementations to disagree, and > rather than >= is the whole difference

cases.name: one cent over the limit is refused
a limit of zero is no limit
cases.why: zero means unset in both engines. An engine that read it as a limit of zero would refuse everything, which is the failure that looks like working enforcement

cases.name: a tiny order against a tiny limit
